title: Dimension bound for the singular locus in a Bertini family
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $Y$ a scheme smooth over $k$, $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module, $V$ a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space of dimension $r$ with a basis $v_1,\dots,v_r$, and $\psi:V\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal L)$ a $k$-linear map. Assume that the sections $\psi(v_1),\dots,\psi(v_r)$ generate $\mathcal L$ and that the associated morphism $\varphi:Y\to\mathbf P^{r-1}_k$ given by $(\psi(v_1):\dots:\psi(v_r))$ is an immersion. Let $H_{\mathrm{univ}}=Z(s_{\mathrm{univ}})\subseteq\mathbf A^r_k\times_kY$ be the zero scheme of the section $s_{\mathrm{univ}}=\sum_{i=1}^rx_i\,\mathrm{pr}_2^*\psi(v_i)$ of $\mathrm{pr}_2^*\mathcal L$, where $x_1,\dots,x_r$ are the coordinates of $\mathbf A^r_k=\operatorname{Spec}k[x_1,\dots,x_r]$, and let $q:H_{\mathrm{univ}}\to\mathbf A^r_k$ be the projection. Let $\Sigma\subseteq H_{\mathrm{univ}}$ be the non-smooth locus of $q$, that is, the set of points $h\in H_{\mathrm{univ}}$ having no open neighbourhood $W\subseteq H_{\mathrm{univ}}$ such that $q|_W:W\to\mathbf A^r_k$ is smooth. Then $\dim(\Sigma)<r$; consequently $q(\Sigma)$ is contained in a proper closed subset $B\subsetneq\mathbf A^r_k$. The scheme, smoothness, immersion, invertible-sheaf, generation, projective-morphism, zero-scheme, base-change and dimension notions are those of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-sc-invertible-module], [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections], [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections], [def-pc-zero-scheme], [def-pc-base-change], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

source.place: Tag 0FD6, lemma-bertini proof: singular-locus dimension estimate

proof.text: If $Y=\varnothing$, then $\Sigma=\varnothing$ and take $B=\varnothing$. This includes $r=0$: generation by no sections forces every stalk of the invertible sheaf to be zero, so there are no points of $Y$. In this case $\mathbf P(V)$ is empty (the usual interpretation of $\mathbf P^{-1}$). Hence assume $Y\ne\varnothing$ and $r\geq1$.

The standard affine charts of $\mathbf P^{r-1}_k$ have finite type coordinate rings, hence Noetherian underlying spaces by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]. Their finite union is Noetherian by [lem-kun-finite-union-noetherian]. An immersion is a homeomorphism onto its locally closed image, so [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets] implies that $Y$ is quasi-compact. Smoothness makes $Y$ locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type; quasi-compactness makes it finite type. The universal zero scheme is finite type: on an affine trivializing open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$ its ring is $A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(\sum x_if_i)$, generated over $k$ by generators of $A$ and the $x_i$. These finitely many charts show that $H_{\mathrm{univ}}$ is finite type. The smooth locus of $q$ is open by the definition of smoothness at a point; thus $\Sigma$ is closed. Give it the reduced closed subscheme structure. On each affine chart this is another quotient of the same finite type algebra, so $\Sigma$ is finite type over $k$.

Cover $Y$ by affine opens $U$ on which $s_i=\psi(v_i)$ trivializes $\mathcal L$ and $\Omega^1_{U/k}$ is free of rank $d$, using [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-differentials-free-rank-fibre-dimension]. Applying its rank equality again at each point of $U$ gives $\dim_u U=d$ everywhere, hence $\dim U=d$. Take a finite such cover using quasi-compactness. Set $f_j=s_j/s_i$, so $f_i=1$. At any $y\in U$, the immersion into the projective chart factors locally as a closed immersion into an open $W\subseteq\mathbf A^{r-1}_k$. Since $U$ is smooth, [lem-pur-conormal-sequence-smooth-immersion] makes $\Omega_{W/k}\otimes\kappa(y)\to\Omega_{U/k}\otimes\kappa(y)$ surjective. The differentials of the affine coordinates generate the source: locally sections on $W$ are polynomial fractions, and $d(a/b)=b^{-1}da-ab^{-2}db$. Their images are $df_j(y)$, $j\ne i$, by the coordinate description of the associated projective morphism. Consequently the residue-field map $E(y):\kappa(y)^r\to\kappa(y)\oplus(\Omega^1_{U/k}\otimes\kappa(y))$, $e_j\mapsto(f_j(y),df_j(y))$, is onto: $e_i$ gives $(1,0)$, and $e_j-f_j(y)e_i$ gives $(0,df_j(y))$. Its rank is therefore $d+1$, so $d+1\leq r$.

On $\mathbf A^r_k\times_kU$ the universal equation is $F=\sum_jx_jf_j$, and its differential relative to $\mathbf A^r_k$ is $dF=\sum_jx_jdf_j$. The ambient projection is smooth, being the base change of $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). The relative differentials here are the pullback of $\Omega^1_{U/k}$: on affine rings the derivations of $k[x]\otimes_k A$ over $k[x]$ are exactly the $k$-derivations of $A$, extended $k[x]$-linearly. If $h\in\Sigma$ lies above $y\in U$, the hypersurface criterion [lem-zl-hypersurface-nonzero-relative-differential] implies $dF(h)=0$, since otherwise $q$ would be smooth at $h$. Also $F(h)=0$ because $h\in H_{\mathrm{univ}}$. Thus $\Sigma\cap p^{-1}(U)$ is contained in the closed locus $K_U$ cut out by $F$ and the $d$ coefficients of $dF$. This is only a containment, and uses no flatness or smoothness assertion about the fibre at the zero coefficient vector.

For every $y\in U$, the fibre $(K_U)_y\subseteq\mathbf A^r_{\kappa(y)}$ is cut out by the homogeneous linear equations $E(y)x=0$. Its matrix has rank $d+1$ by Step 3. Choose a nonzero maximal minor and solve for the corresponding $d+1$ variables; the other $r-d-1$ variables are free, giving $(K_U)_y\cong\mathbf A^{r-d-1}_{\kappa(y)}$. The polynomial dimension formula [lem-sf-noetherian-polynomial-dimension], with the spectrum/ring identification [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring], gives fibre dimension $r-d-1$. Here a field has dimension zero because its only prime is $(0)$. Since $U$ is affine finite type of dimension $d$ and $K_U$ is the closed subscheme defined by these finitely many equations in $\mathbf A^r\times U$, the fibre bound in [lem-zl-finite-type-fibre-image-dimension-bounds] gives $\dim K_U\leq d+(r-d-1)=r-1$. A closed subspace cannot increase dimension: a chain of irreducible closed subsets remains such a chain in its ambient space. Hence Step 4 gives $\dim(\Sigma\cap p^{-1}(U))\leq r-1$.

These opens cover $\Sigma$, so $\dim\Sigma\leq r-1<r$. Explicitly, for a chain of irreducible closed subsets of $\Sigma$, choose one of the opens meeting its smallest member. All members meet that open and their intersections remain irreducible and closed there; strictness is preserved, since a nonempty open in an irreducible space is dense and therefore cannot be contained in a proper closed subset. Thus every chain has length at most $r-1$. Apply the image inequality in [lem-zl-finite-type-fibre-image-dimension-bounds] to $q|_\Sigma:\Sigma\to\mathbf A^r_k$: $B=\overline{q(\Sigma)}$ has dimension at most $\dim\Sigma<r$. The polynomial dimension formula and the spectrum/ring identification give $\dim\mathbf A^r_k=r$, so $B$ is a proper closed subset containing $q(\Sigma)$.

The first-order surjectivity detail is written out from the existing conormal sequence, avoiding an elementary new node.

Source error: 0FD6 proves flatness only over an open U but uses 'q smooth at (x,v) iff H_v smooth at x' for every v. I confirmed the report's counterexample by hand: Y=A^1 with sections 1,t gives q=(-bt,b), which is not flat at the origin while H_0 is smooth. The repair uses only the true direction (nonzero relative dF gives smoothness), so Sigma lies in {F=dF=0}. This keeps the route and is openly marked agent. Steps 1-6: Step 1 handles empty Y and r=0. Step 2 gets quasi-compactness of Y from the Noetherian projective space plus the immersion, so Y is finite type. Step 3: free Omega charts with constant d; the conormal surjection; e_i gives (1,0) and e_j-f_je_i gives (0,df_j), so the rank is d+1 and d+1<=r. Step 4: smooth base change (lem-pc-proper-base-change(2), Lean-closed) and the hypersurface node, all hypotheses met. Step 5: fibres of K_U are A^{r-d-1} over kappa(y); the fibre bound gives dim K_U<=r-1. Step 6: the finite chain argument and the image-closure bound give dim B<r=dim A^r. New nodes: the hypersurface criterion is true (one Jacobian row added to a standard smooth presentation, then 00T7), tested on t-a, at and t^p-a. It is not a duplicate: the trf smooth-at-point criterion needs flatness and the RGCI Jacobian node needs a global presentation. The fibre/image dimension bounds are true via 0B2L(2)(a) on finitely many components and not a duplicate (I checked the zl lower-bound, kun dimension formula and sbc flat fibre-dimension nodes). Both are statement-only, with all three search kinds, correct blueprint.from/via and same_as [].
